attacksRun.evidence: The gating test, run against live harness bytes rather than against my own v1 text. SF1 demanded each of the two classes carry at least one named initial state DRAWN FROM G19 v1 exactByteIntent, with NOT-AUTHORED attached to those named states rather than to the class name, and it identified the available material as the two state-classes crossed with the four lifecycle operations plus file 04's four named negative tests. v2 delivers exactly that: 12 states, 8 for class-lifecycle-matrix and 4 for cross-class-mutations. The 8 are the complete 2x4 cross product of includedPreviewClasses (Rebuildable cache/index, Operational metadata) with lifecycleOperations (migration, backup, purge, recovery); both class names appear verbatim in the live matrix exactByteIntent and the live slash-joined set '{migration, backup, purge, recovery}' is present there verbatim. The 4 are cross-class writes, cache-to-authority promotion, undeclared Plan inputs, and component evidence commits — all four verbatim in the live cross-class-mutations exactByteIntent. Every record carries stateNamed plus a source field, and fixtureBytes NOT-AUTHORED now hangs off the named state. The v1 shape was four fields; v2 carries six. SF1 is landed.

attacksRun.attack: the live platform axis is not carried onto the matrix states (my own attack)
attacksRun.evidence: The sharpest residual point. Live matrix exactByteIntent scopes cells 'on each D-002 platform' and its passProperty requires every included-class x operation cell 'on all four D-002 platforms', so a fully enumerated matrix would be 2 x 4 x 4 = 32 rather than the 8 named here; the states carry no platform field at all. I decline to charge it: nothing false is asserted, because whatIsAuthored says precisely 'eight included-class x lifecycle-operation cells and four named negative tests' and never claims platform completeness or exhaustiveness; the governing platform requirement sits in G19 v1 and the named catalog, both pinned here at verified digests; and SF1's stated repair was the two state-classes crossed with the four lifecycle operations, which is delivered exactly. Recorded for two reasons: a later fixture-authoring cycle must carry the platform axis forward, and the sibling g16-input-corpus.v2 reviewed in this same chain DID carry a platforms field, so a coordinator may want one convention across the input-corpus family.

observationsNotFindings: The 8 matrix states carry no platform field although live G19 v1 scopes cells 'on each D-002 platform' and its passProperty requires all four. Nothing false is asserted — whatIsAuthored claims exactly eight class x operation cells and no exhaustiveness — but a later fixture-authoring cycle must carry the platform axis forward.

The two input corpora therefore differ on whether the platform axis is materialised. Neither is defective on its own terms; a single convention across the family would be cleaner.

All cited digests recomputed clean; HEAD 5d5d778; required-now 26.
